subject: Number of PIT values and residuals

messages.author: c38694fbd65acb1d
messages.subject: Number of PIT values and residuals
parts:
Dear everyone,

I am fitting a model with spatial data and frailties thanks to INLA. In order to test the validity of the model, I want to plot the histogram of PIT values. My database has 6,071 observations but the algorithm calculates 24,339 values, but I don't understand why because I thought there was 1 PIT value for each observation. Do you have any suggestion ?
Moreover, how can I plot Cox-Snell residuals and Martingale residuals ?

All the best and thank you in advance,
Edwige

messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Number of PIT values and residuals
parts: Moreover, how can I plot Cox-Snell residuals and Martingale residuals ?

I believe that Wang et al. [1] describe Cox-Snell residuals. You can also check the R code of our paper on survival models with INLA [2,3] to see how we have implemented them using iNLA. Not sure about martingale residuals but I am sure that you can implement them using the INLA output and, if needed, sampling.

Best,

Virgilio


[1] https://www.routledge.com/Bayesian-Regression-Modeling-with-INLA/Wang-Ryan-Faraway/p/book/9780367572266

[2] https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1177/1471082X20967158

[3] https://github.com/rsbivand/survival_katrina

Hi, 

Thank you for your help ! I tried to use the package brinla (bri.surv.resid and bri.csresid.plot) in order to plot Cox-Snell residuals but the first function returns the following error : "maximum number of subdivisions reached", so I tried to change arguments within the function (subdivisions = 1000, stop.on.error = FALSE) but I still have an error : "non-finite function value". How can I solve this problem ?

Best,
Edwige
